# S51 — run.json at 0600; strip control characters from recorded commands

S45 review (2026-10-20): internal/runrec/store.go writes run.json at 0644, and a recorded denied command can hold a secret (capped at 200 characters, not scrubbed). Only CR and LF are replaced, so ESC and other control characters reach ork status and the TUI. Decided #106 (state.run-json-mode): write run.json and the run directory files at 0600 and strip all control characters from a recorded command. The raw stdout of a denied round is already 0600 (docs/design.md:372).

**Findings:**  · **Size:** S · **Tree:**

**Not in this slice:**

## Why

A recorded command can hold a secret and can hold terminal escape sequences. #106 decided both fixes.

## Files

- internal/runrec (store, record), the code that builds the recorded text (internal/agent/claude/types.go), tests, docs/state.md.

## Failing tests

- run.json and the other files ork writes in a run directory are created 0600, and an existing 0644 file is written back at 0600.
- A recorded command with ESC, NUL, TAB or other control characters has them removed (CR and LF still become spaces first); printable text is unchanged.
- The 200-character cap still holds after stripping.
- Existing run records still load.
- docs/state.md states the file mode.
